title: Cundinamarca
capsule: The Free and Independent State of Cundinamarca was a short-lived republic centered on Bogotá, proclaimed during the chaos of New Granada's independence struggle against Spain. In August 1813 it declared full independence, and its leader Antonio Nariño was named dictator to prosecute a southern campaign that briefly took Popayán before defeat at Pasto in May 1814 led to his capture and imprisonment in Spain. Simón Bolívar compelled Bogotá's submission in December 1814, folding Cundinamarca into the United Provinces of New Granada; Spanish forces under Pablo Morillo completed the reconquest on 6 May 1816.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is reasonably attested for its Bogotá-centered core, but the precise boundaries of jurisdiction during the brief 1813–1815 period are not consistently mapped in the scholarly literature.
